findings.title: OR auth fragment is not fully parenthesized, so extra AND filters skip team bookings
findings.body: Team and org authorization SQL is built as `(<team predicate>) OR (<user predicate>)` (org reduce at lines 171-174, team reduce at lines 204-207). Those parentheses wrap each branch only, not the whole OR. `getBaseConditions` returns that fragment as-is when there is no event-type or member filter (line 75). AND binds tighter than OR in PostgreSQL, so the intended caller query `WHERE ${await service.getBaseConditions()} AND "startTime" >= ${from} AND "startTime" < ${to}` — the replacement for the removed `findMany`, which ANDed caller filters onto the entire authorization object — is parsed as `team_booking_predicate OR (personal_booking_predicate AND startTime filters)`. Every team booking for that team or org is included no matter what date, status, or other AND predicates the caller adds. Insights over-count and can return bookings outside the window the caller applied. `getBaseConditions` only wraps the auth fragment when a service-level filter is also present (line 73). Wrap the full OR, and the final fragment returned to callers, in parentheses. The new tests expect this unparenthesized text and never run team/org SQL with an additional AND, so they do not catch it.

findings.title: toEqual(Prisma.sql) does not match nested SQL fragments
findings.body: Composed conditions are built by nesting `Prisma.sql` values (`(${acc}) OR (${condition})` and the filter AND reduce). Prisma does not flatten nested `strings`/`values` until execution, so the object from `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` is not deeply equal to a single flat `Prisma.sql` template with the same text. `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)` therefore fails for the team-scope assertion (line 295), the org-scope assertion (line 332), and the combined-filter assertion (line 429) — the cases that use `ANY(...)` and OR. Flat cases (user scope, a single filter, `1=0`) can still pass. The only test that executes SQL is the user-scope `$queryRaw` query, which never hits `ANY` or the OR precedence bug. Compare flattened SQL text and bound values, or run the team/org fragments, instead of `toEqual` on raw `Prisma.Sql` objects.
